newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up as market eyes company results.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up as market eyes company results.

text.p: Share prices on the Lima Stock Exchange closed fractionally higher in moderate trade on Thursday with investors still eyeing movements on Wall Street and forthcoming company results, brokers said.
Stocks were expected to end the week little changed as investors bided their time before taking new positions, they added.
"The U.S. unemployment rate comes out tomorrow and if the rate is high the Dow Jones could fall more steeply, and that could affect us," said Luis Cueva of the Argos brokerage.
The bolsa's General Index rose 0.32 percent to 1,664.91 points while the blue-chip Selective Index was up 0.45 percent at 2,392.67 points.
Turnover was 31.8 million soles ($11.9 million) on 1,562 trades.
A steady trickle of positive first quarter results, particularly for mining companies, was expected to boost the market in coming weeks, brokers said.
"It is said that the mining companies' balances will be good and Telefonica is also expected to be positive. This will help the market's long-term propects," Cueva said.

Bellwether Telefonica del Peru "B" shares rose 0.66 percent to 6.06 soles on 2,171,770 shares. Cement company Cementos Lima also rose 1.12 percent to 4.50 soles on 40.580 shares, reflecting expectations of improved macro-economic growth, brokers said.
Mining stocks closed mostly off with Atacocha down 0.95 percent at 1.04 soles on 140,649 shares, and Morococha slipping 0.90 percent to 2.21 soles on 60,337 shares.
Mining company prospects were, however, basically strong and unlikely to be affected by small bouts of profit taking, brokers said.
